notes: Full sweep 2026-10-31-b: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Each result.json has head 74112b4, uncommitted false, skill_hash f2dfc909..., rc 0 and model_id equal to the requested model. Every assistant message in each transcript reports only the run's model. Each transcript contains the current sentence "A `for` reads the same way" and none contains the removed "A `for` always takes", so the runs read the current skill. All five read both expected reference files before writing review.md (haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 with `cat`), and opus-1 and sonnet-2 also read library-design.md. Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex. Opus-1 built a test project inside its run folder and deleted it before finishing. Haiku-2 wrote a check copy of the importer in its run folder, ran the format check and a compile against stand-in modules, and deleted it. Haiku-1's extraction commands were refused, and its review says it did not compile or format (line 174). Sonnet-1 tried neither and says so (line 3). Sonnet-2 also wrote improved.ex, which is byte-identical to its review block; result.json records format_ok true for it and compiles false, and the compile error is only the missing `Accounts.User` struct, since the same code compiles without warnings beside a schema in this grade's run. Only sonnet-2's result.json has format_ok, so the other four come from this grade's own check.

Rule list: the same 16 index rows as the 2026-10-31 grades. git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes none of them. It adds the `for` sentences to 'One expression per line, and tabular clauses', drops the `for` sentence and example from the `do:` rule, changes the macro rules in macros.md and adds one, and shortens an ETS example in processes.md. No output contains a `for`, so those `for` sentences are not exercised, and no output contains a macro or ETS table. All 16 rules are graded to the 2026-10-31 standard: a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it. A silent fix, or a mention only under behaviour changes or assumptions, does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported. The nesting belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'. The comments, both magic numbers and a dropped line 11 why-comment belong to 'Comments explain why...'. Input lines 12 and 55 belong to the pipeline rule. The line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors belong to 'Match every expected shape'; a finding that treats the rescue only as hiding bugs does not count for the identical errors. The line 8 raise and the `try/rescue` with `String.to_integer/1` belong to 'Return {:ok, value}...'. The dead `is_binary` belongs to no rule. A one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body is not nesting. An assumed or companion changeset counts as a changeset. String-key reads in a body are not counted under the required-keys rule, whose sentences are about atom keys and structs. The sentence "Include `## Examples` that work as doctests." decides no verdict: none of the five outputs has an `## Examples` section, and earlier code-review grades gave 'Comments explain why...' clean to runs without one.

Planted problems, mapped as in the 2026-10-31 grades: 21 problems from the case table's 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding counted apart from the magic 120, and the line 49 spawn apart from the closure copy. Counts: opus-1 21/21. Haiku-1 16/21, missing the `try/rescue` with `String.to_integer/1`, both magic numbers, the dead `is_binary` and the identical errors. Haiku-2 18/21, missing the dead `is_binary`, the overlapping options and the identical errors. Sonnet-1 18/21, missing the dead `is_binary`, the identical errors and the closure copy. Sonnet-2 18/21, missing the line 12 single-step pipe, the magic 18 and the closure copy. All five report the line 24 lookup-before-insert with the race and drop `Repo.get_by/2` for `unique_constraint(:email)`: opus-1 finding 4, haiku-1 finding 5, haiku-2 finding 5, sonnet-1 finding 4 and sonnet-2 finding 9.

Judgment calls on 'reported'. Haiku-2's line 8 raise counts through finding 10 (line 23), and this is borderline. The finding quotes `params["role"]` at line 8 and describes a late confusing error, not a raise outside the `try`, but its stated fix, a second clause returning `{:error, :invalid_payload}` for input without the required keys, addresses a missing role, and the run returns that error. So 'Return {:ok, value}...' is clean for haiku-2. The Haiku tier result would be the same either way, since haiku-1 violates that rule. Haiku-2's finding 2 reports both magic numbers ("The 120 and 18 are also magic numbers."); the 120 becomes `@max_age` and the 18 moves to an assumed changeset that the review does not show, so no literal 18 is in its code, though the assumption on line 37 still states it. Haiku-1's finding 3 gives no name for the 120, unlike the finding that counted in 2026-10-31, and `@max_age` (line 68) is a silent fix. Sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's 120 count through their fixes, which name `@max_age` (sonnet-1 findings 3 and 13, sonnet-2 finding 4). Haiku-1 (finding 7, line 35), haiku-2 (finding 3, line 9) and sonnet-1 (finding 2, line 9) do not count for the identical errors: the first covers only input line 33, and the other two treat the rescue only as hiding bugs, as 2026-10-31 judged. Haiku-1's line 167 mentions the old atoms under behaviour changes, which does not count. Sonnet-2 counts through finding 17 (line 39). Haiku-1's finding 11 ("One function does four jobs at four levels of nesting") counts for the nesting, and so does haiku-2's finding 7 ("the `if`/`case` nesting in lines 15-41"). Sonnet-1's finding 10 and sonnet-2's finding 13 name only the missing supervisor, and both programs still capture `user` in the closure, so here the copy is both unreported and present in the code.

False positives: haiku-2 finding 4 (line 11) and sonnet-2 finding 6 (line 17) put must-not-report line 27 `opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]` under the `and`/`or`/`not` rule beside line 21, and sonnet-1 finding 7 (line 19) does the same through its title's `!`, which occurs only on line 27. None changes a verdict on that rule, since all three report line 21. Haiku-2 goes further than the sonnets: its fix applies the operators, line 70 `if opts[:notify] and not opts[:silent], do: send_welcome(user)`. Line 66 gives both options boolean defaults, so no `and` or `not` falls on a nil-able option and the no-options call returns normally. Haiku-2 never names the overlap and keeps both options, so 'Use one atom-valued field or option instead of overlapping booleans' is violated. Opus-1 (finding 11) and haiku-1 (finding 8) treat line 27 only as overlapping options. No run reports line 19, and every run keeps the line 11 why-comment (opus-1 line 135, haiku-1 line 108, haiku-2 line 86, sonnet-1 line 69, sonnet-2 line 110). Sonnet-1's finding 14 (line 33) splits `alias Accounts.{Repo, User}` under no rule; that line is not on the must-not-report list, so it is recorded only under the finding-format check.

Rules outside the list, checked against their current text. 'Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call': haiku-2 lines 89-94 spread a four-entry map that takes 94 columns on one line, so it is listed under other_violations, decided by "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." The 2026-10-31 grades did not list the same shape in sonnet-2's lines 108-113, which took 88 columns, so this listing is new. It affects no verdict, and I list it because the brief asks for any other rule seen broken. Haiku-1's `user_attrs/1` map (lines 100-105) takes 116 columns on one line, so it stays spread. The `->` rule: haiku-2 lines 79-81 keep three one-line clauses, each returning a finished tagged tuple, so "each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern" allows them; this differs from 2026-10-31's sonnet-2, whose first clause continued the computation. The `with` rule: opus-1 line 81 and haiku-1 lines 83 and 94 are one-step pass-through `with`s with no `else`, which the rule allows, and the other runs have two or three steps. 'Parse external data into structs where it enters the system': haiku-1 lines 98, 102 and 103 read required string keys and pass them to a changeset whose `validate_required/2` reports a missing one; the sentence forbids reading each key and checking for `nil`, so it is not listed. Haiku-2 and sonnet-1 call a four-argument private `insert_user/4`; no earlier grade listed a private function of that size under 'Group related parameters', so it is not listed. Every `do:` body is one expression on the head's line and every `fn` holds one call; sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's multi-line `fn` would pass 98 columns on one line. No block compiles with a warning, so 'Before you finish' is not listed for any run. Haiku-1 and sonnet-1 did not compile, and the review.md output is not an Elixir file, as in 2026-10-31.

Format check: each review.md's elixir blocks were extracted to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suazi-Repos-idiomatic-elixir-skill/63fbd3f7-5995-424e-b268-7679cfbb08c1/scratchpad/grade-scratch-b/code-review-skill/blocks/<run>-block<N>.ex. Elixir 1.20.3's `mix format --check-formatted` exits 0 on every importer block and on sonnet-1's changeset snippet. Opus-1's and haiku-1's block2 schemas fail only because a bare file lacks Ecto's `locals_without_parens` for `field`; with a .formatter.exs giving those (ectofmt/) they exit 0. A misformatted control (bad.ex) exits 1. So format_ok is true for all five.

No-options check: each importer was run against real Ecto 3.14.2 (Mix.install) by /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suazi-Repos-idiomatic-elixir-skill/63fbd3f7-5995-424e-b268-7679cfbb08c1/scratchpad/grade-scratch-b/code-review-skill/drive/run.exs, using common.exs (an `Accounts.Repo.insert/1` stub that applies the changeset action, plus `Mailer` and `Accounts.Mailer` stubs that message the driver) and a real `Accounts.TaskSupervisor`. Opus-1 and haiku-1 use their own schema block; sonnet-1 uses its own changeset in a grader schema; haiku-2 and sonnet-2 use the changeset their reviews assume. In all five, `import_user(%{"email" => "Ann@Example.com", "age" => "130", "role" => "admin"})` with no options returns `{:ok, user}` with age 120 and a lowercased email and sends no mail. With `notify: true` it delivers exactly one email. An age of 17, an unknown role, a missing role, a missing email and age "abc" each return `{:error, _}`. No block gives a compiler warning. The stub Repo has no database, so `unique_constraint/3` was not exercised. Extra probe, outside the standard and deciding no verdict: a JSON number age and a number email raise `FunctionClauseError` in haiku-2 (lines 78, 87), although its `@doc` promises an error tuple when age is not an integer string. The other four return an error or, for opus-1 and haiku-1, accept the number age.

Compared with the 2026-10-31 skill grade, per_rule changes in five of the 16 rows. Haiku goes from violated to clean on the required-keys rule, 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...' (both haikus now read the struct by dot and name the nesting), and from clean to violated on 'Use one atom-valued field or option...' (haiku-2 keeps `silent`).
